analysis:
The only changed file is the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. The change adds a StubTokenizer.decodeTable (head lines ~146-155), a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge test helper (~443, 462), and new tests at lines 847-899. These tests cover scoped stop-string matching: the matched-sequence report names the exact candidate, a stop never matches inside a reasoning span, and a request-level scope replaces the model-level scope. No production code is changed in the supplied units, so no change to a trust boundary, a key, encryption, authorization or attestation is visible here.

The tests also pin existing security-relevant behaviors. Caller-controlled prompt_cache_key and user fields never become cacheSalt; only the explicitly passed cacheScope becomes the salt (lines 761-785). This matches the T-041 mitigation that the coordinator authors the scope. Usage can only be raised, never lowered, which is the billing-zero defense (lines 1062-1073). Telemetry carries fixed keys only and never the raw engine message. The retired env-key test confirms the SSD prefix-cache envs stay live (lines 1717-1726).

The production side of the stop-scope change (EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with a scope, and ReasoningStopScope) is outside the supplied units. I could not check the bridge implementation; any impact on stop-string handling or on the reported matchedStopSequence in usage signals needs the source-side review. Nothing in the tests suggests a regression.
